incident_spec.summary: Excessive creation of temporary tables on disk in MySQL due to query patterns and configuration limits.
symptoms: High percentage of temporary tables created on disk.
Performance concerns related to disk-based temporary tables.
incident_spec.mechanism: MySQL creates temporary tables on disk when certain conditions are met, such as the presence of TEXT/BLOB fields, exceeding tmp_table_size or max_heap_table_size, or using large columns with GROUP BY, UNION, or ORDER BY.

facts.evidence: Configuration details provided in the post.
Answer 1 mentions TEXT/BLOB fields and large columns as contributors.

assumptions: Queries involve TEXT/BLOB fields or large columns.
The workload includes GROUP BY, UNION, or ORDER BY operations.
unknowns: Exact query patterns causing the issue.
Whether the database schema includes TEXT/BLOB fields or large columns.

feasibility.rationale: The mechanism of disk-based temporary table creation can be reproduced by simulating queries with TEXT/BLOB fields and large columns exceeding tmp_table_size or max_heap_table_size.

schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS large_table (id INT PRIMARY KEY, large_text_field TEXT, large_blob_field BLOB, category VARCHAR(64), payload VARCHAR(255))
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS small_table (id INT PRIMARY KEY, ref_id INT, name VARCHAR(64))
generation_sql: INSERT INTO small_table (id, ref_id, name) SELECT n, MOD(n, 10), CONCAT('name_', n) FROM generated_numbers WHERE n <= 100

INSERT INTO large_table (id, large_text_field, large_blob_field, category, payload) SELECT n, REPEAT('text_', n % 10), REPEAT('blob_', n % 10), CASE WHEN MOD(n, 1000)=0 THEN 'rare' ELSE 'common' END, CONCAT('payload_', n) FROM generated_numbers WHERE n <= {row_count}
